questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: First the fact that Austria was not a long way from my home country. Second that german is spoken (I would like to improve my german skills). Third that UNI Wien offered a lot of English law courses.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was quite easy. The UNI Wien website is user-friendly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I attended an orientation session.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I think there was a lot of options. 
HousingAnyWhere, Airbnb and also CoLivi Wien (where I rented by apartment).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed living in my own apartment, so I had my own space. And I lived in the 4th District, which was really nice, close to the inner city but still very peaceful. Dont be afraid of living alone, there is plenty opportunities to get to know people through ESN / EBN and also just attending to courses at UNI.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy ? Ufind - was brilliant !

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: U basically just register through u:space (it is very easy), and you can look up all the courses at Ufind.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You have the possibility to call the UNI (which I also did, and they were very helpful).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that I wanted. I registered for 60 ECTS to be sure to get 30 ECTS, but that wasnt necessary at all ! But it is always possible to deregister.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I only registered for classes with Continuous assessment of course work, those courses have mandatory attending but then you dont have big exams in the middle of July. In some of my courses, I only had to deliver in two assignments. And in most of my classes we would just have an exam in the last class.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was lots easier than in Denmark ! The level is still fine, but it is easier. I also think it has to do with, that the English courses at UNI Wien are 3-4 ECTS only. And then most courses dont have heavy reading.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UNI Wien we didn't have lectures. But only classes, which was nice. So the students were very engaged in the classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- International Investment Law 
- International Economic Law
- International Protection of Cultural Heritage
- International Legal English
- Women in Law part 2 
- Drafting and Negotiating Cross-border M & A and Joint Venture Contracts
- Introduction to US Law
- Protection of Intellectual Properties in the Fashion Industry.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I believe that the International Legal English course is great, since it is extremely relevant for all exchange students. I also found International Protection of Cultural Heritage interesting and also Protection of Intellectual Properties in the Fashion Industry, since it is not possible to do such courses at my home university. 

In general I really enjoyed all my courses.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really any.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
I was surprised that we didnt have to buy any books. So a great advice, even though the courses are provided with a reading list, you dont have to buy them, since the will provide pdf or online book.

And also you can buy a semester ticket at WienMobil for the public transport, which covers free transport within Wien for only 75 EUR for the whole semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: UNI Wien has USI which is a sports institution, which really offers ALL you can think of. The have a really nice Welcoming reception at the begining of each semester for exchange students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Lots are avaliable  - ESN and also EBN organises events all the time. Check their websites out. For example both organisations are doing a ski trip, hikes, parties, board game nights, pubcrawls, museum visits, BBQ etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
- See a museum (Wien has a lot to offer example SISI museum, National Museum of Art, Upper Belevedere)
- Go for a walk in the Schönbrunen Castle Park and even see the museum inside.
- Go for a walk in the inner city and enjoy all the pretty buildings - hofburg palace, the opera, Stephansdom etc.)
- Go to Gerstner in the inner city (next to the Opera) and eat cake while enjoying the outstanding interior.
- Do a picnic in Volksgarten or Burggarten.
- Go swim at the Donau Island
- Go for a Hike through Vienna and up to the Wine marks (example Mayer am Nussberg)
- Take a trip for skiing (maybe Zell am see) or hiking - or just to see some big Austrian mountains.
- Take a trip to Budapest (only 2,5 hours in train)
- Take a trip to Bratislava (less than 1 hour in train)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, Austria is not that different from Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Really just use ESN and EBN !! Then you will meet other people. And then make sure to become a member of the whatsapp group of ESN UNI Wien, people write all the time, and there are so many people, who would like to do stuff.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People were very polite.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
(1) Dont be nervous to spend some time alone in the beginning. It is normal to feel overwhelmed, and there will come plenty of social activities that you can attend to.
(2) Think of that you are all in the same spot. Every Erasmus student has an interest in getting to know new people.
(3) Believe in yourself, it will all be great ! And it is going to be one of your biggest experiences in life.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think it has been written in this report.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: That I realized that I am capable of so much more, than I thought. Sometimes I was very out of comfort zone.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To try and live alone and just stand on one's own feet.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
